Border-less Card for Chart and Table Combined Output

Source: R/crukChartTable.R
crukChartTable.Rd

Creates a border-less bslib card with two panels: one for a chart and the other for a table. This function has a requirement for alt text to ensure accessibility best practice.

Usage

crukChartTable(
  chart,
  table,
  alt,
  dataSourceText = NULL,
  dataSourceLink = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

chart

A chart output in the form of a shiny::plotOutput, plotly::plotlyOutput, or highcharter::highchartOutput.

table

A table output in the form of a shiny::tableOutput, DT::dataTableOutput, gt::gt_output, or reactable::reactableOutput.

alt

Character. Alt text to include alongside the chart. Minimum 15 characters; over 125 characters gives a warning (it may cause issues with some screen readers). Please ensure alt text is sufficiently descriptive. Supplied character string will be appended with the text " Please see table for the data in an accessible format."

dataSourceText

Optional. Character, or a shiny.tag/UI output object (e.g. shiny::textOutput, shiny::uiOutput). The data source text displayed at the bottom of the table, after a static "Data source: " label on the same line. If a tag/output object is supplied it is inserted as rendered content rather than coerced to a string. Top-level div outputs (the default for textOutput and uiOutput) are converted to spans so they stay inline. If NULL (the default), no data source line is added and "Data source" does not appear.

dataSourceLink

Optional. Where the user goes when they click dataSourceText. Either a single character URL, or a shiny.tag output (shiny::textOutput or shiny::uiOutput) whose rendered content is the URL, so the link can be reactive. The URL is never displayed. For a renderUI output you can return plain text, or a tag containing an <a href>, in which case its href is used. Only http(s):// URLs are used; if the rendered value is anything else the text is shown without a link. Needs dataSourceText: if supplied on its own, it is ignored with a warning.

...

Optional additional arguments

Value

A bslib::navset_card_tab object with attached CSS dependencies for CRUK styling. The card includes:

  • A border-less, shadow-less card with two bslib::nav_panels

  • A tab with the heading "Chart".

  • Attached alt text to the chart output, directing users to the table

  • A tab with the heading "Table" and, if supplied, a data source

  • Optional additional arguments placed above the card, e.g. a title using htmltools::h1 or selectors using shinyCRUK::crukPickerInput or shinyCRUK::crukSelectInput.

Usage Tips

  • Use descriptive but concise alt text

  • By default, plotly::plotlyOutputs should scale to fill the div, so avoid manually setting chart sizes

  • If you want a title or selectors to apply to the chart and table, pass these as additional arguments. They will be displayed about the chart table card

  • Ideally give full data source. If this is not possible (for example because you are using UK data from several sources), then you can direct the user to a data sources/references box at the bottom of the page and supply the function the full URL of the app with the div id of the data sources/reference box

  • dataSourceText can be a dynamic shiny::textOutput or shiny::uiOutput if you need the data source label to update reactively; just remember to bind it server-side with a matching output$id <- renderText({...}) (or renderUI), since the output tag itself is only a placeholder until bound.

  • dataSourceLink is the destination of the click on dataSourceText; the URL itself is never shown.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Basic card with just chart and table
crukChartTable(
  chart = plotlyOutput(outputId = "mtcarsPlot"),
  table = gt::gt_output(outputId = "mtTable"),
  alt = "A chart showing how horsepower varies according to mpg in the mtcars dataset."
)

# Card with a data source
crukChartTable(
  chart = plotlyOutput(outputId = "mtcarsPlot"),
  table = gt::gt_output(outputId = "mtTable"),
  alt = "A chart showing how horsepower varies according to mpg in the mtcars dataset.",
  dataSourceText = "mtcars: Motor Trend Car Road Tests",
  dataSourceLink = "https://www.rdocumentation.org/packages/datasets/versions/3.6.2/topics/mtcars"
)

# Chart and table card with additional arguments passed
crukChartTable(
  chart = plotlyOutput(outputId = "mtcarsPlot"),
  table = gt::gt_output(outputId = "mtTable"),
  alt = "Some alt text to go with the chart.",
  dataSourceText = "mtcars: Motor Trend Car Road Tests",
  dataSourceLink = "https://www.rdocumentation.org/packages/datasets/versions/3.6.2/topics/mtcars",
  htmltools::h1("mtcars: higher horsepower decreases mpg"),
  htmltools::br(),
  prettyCheckbox(inputId = "showCIs",
                 label = strong("Show confidence intervals"),
                 shape = "square",
                 value = FALSE)
)

# Chart and table card with a reactive data source label
crukChartTable(
  chart = plotlyOutput(outputId = "mtcarsPlot"),
  table = gt::gt_output(outputId = "mtTable"),
  alt = "Some alt text to go with the chart.",
  dataSourceText = shiny::textOutput("dataSourceLabel"),
  dataSourceLink = "https://www.rdocumentation.org/packages/datasets/versions/3.6.2/topics/mtcars"
)

# Chart and table card with a reactive data source label and link.
# Server side: output$dataSourceLabel <- renderText(...);
#              output$dataSourceUrl <- renderText(url())
crukChartTable(
  chart = plotlyOutput(outputId = "mtcarsPlot"),
  table = gt::gt_output(outputId = "mtTable"),
  alt = "Some alt text to go with the chart.",
  dataSourceText = shiny::textOutput("dataSourceLabel"),
  dataSourceLink = shiny::textOutput("dataSourceUrl")
)
} # }
